decisions.reason: As a low-maintenance utility web service that fits the firm's software/API profile, it is likely to be retained unless demand has proven too weak.
This is a very niche, country-specific regulatory database, so a medium-sized consultancy would likely discontinue it if it did not generate steady recurring business.
The service is specialized and likely project-driven, making it a plausible candidate to be withdrawn if customer uptake has remained limited.
A tariff database requires continuous data maintenance, and a consultancy would usually keep it only if subscription demand clearly covers that effort.
Custom web services are closely aligned with the firm's core consulting and development business, so management would be inclined to continue offering them.
A postal code lookup service is a standard supporting web service with modest operating cost and reasonable fit to the firm's broader software offering.
